Title: PRE-FLIGHT -- Returns Module Installed, Return Setting On, return-attachments Upload Scope Configured (Suite BLOCKED, Not FAIL, When Any Is Missing)
Preconditions:
Runner-native. No browser. Nothing is created except one unattached probe file. ENVIRONMENT REQUIRED BY THIS SUITE (a miss here makes the suite BLOCKED, never FAIL):
(1) Module VirtoCommerce.Return installed (GET /api/platform/modules, isInstalled=true).
(2) Store {{STORE_ID}} Settings > Return > Return: "Return module" (Return.ReturnEnabled) = ON; "Order statuses allowing returns" (Return.AllowedOrderStatuses) contains Completed; "Return window, days" (Return.WindowDays) = 30; "Photos or documents required" (Return.AttachmentsRequired) = ON (the create cases attach one file per line); "Return reasons" (Return.Reasons) contains NoLongerNeeded.
(3) Platform configuration FileUpload:Scopes includes return-attachments (without it POST /api/files/return-attachments is refused and every create case cannot attach).
(4) Seeded fixtures: npm run seed:returns (RETURNS_ORDER_*) and npm run seed:returns:decisions (RETURNS_AUTH_JOURNEY) — check with npm run returns:check / npm run returns:decisions:check; buyer {{USER_EMAIL}} and agent {{ADMIN}} (holds return:authorize); colleague {{USER2_EMAIL}} in the SAME organization (RETURNS_COLLEAGUE).
Steps:
[AUTH role=ADMIN_DEFAULT]
[REST-OP modules]
GET {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/modules
[REST-EXEC modules]
[AUTH role=USER]
[GQL-OP policy]
query { returnPolicy(storeId: "{{STORE_ID}}") { isEnabled windowDays allowedOrderStatuses } }
[GQL-EXEC policy]
[REST-OP upload_probe]
POST {{BACK_URL}}/api/files/return-attachments
Content-Type: multipart/form-data
Body: file=@@td(UPLOAD_FIXTURES.primary.path) (mimeType: image/png; filename: Logo1.png)
[REST-EXEC upload_probe]
[REST-CAPTURE upload_probe.body.[0].url → PROBE_URL]
Assertions:
[ERRORS label=modules] HTTP 200
[DATA label=modules] body.[?title=Returns].isInstalled = true
[ERRORS label=policy] errors[] empty
[DATA label=policy] data.returnPolicy.isEnabled = true
[ERRORS label=upload_probe] HTTP 200
[DATA label=upload_probe] body.[0].url is non-null
[EVIDENCE] BLOCKED guard: every assertion in this case is an ENVIRONMENT prerequisite. A failure here means the stand is not prepared (module absent, store Return module setting off, FileUpload:Scopes without return-attachments) and the whole suite must be reported BLOCKED with the failing prerequisite named - it is not a product FAIL and no later case in this suite is meaningful.
Cross_Layer_Checks: [REST] evidence is the graphql-runner JSON per label; the probe file is left unattached (no return references it)
Failure_Signals: modules does not list VirtoCommerce.Return as installed; returnPolicy.isEnabled=false (Settings > Return > Return > "Return module" is off for the store); the upload probe is refused (platform FileUpload:Scopes lacks return-attachments) - each means SUITE BLOCKED, environment to be fixed, not a defect
Cleanup: none -- the probe upload is unreferenced

Title: returnReasons -- localizedName Is Per-Culture Admin Text With Code Fallback, Not A Single Global String
Preconditions: Runner-native. No browser. RET-GQL-010 asserted only en-US, where D4 (the domain map's own finding) reported EVERY code's localizedName byte-identical to its code -- indistinguishable from a lookup that always falls back, never actually translating anything. Two translations were since entered into the admin dictionary specifically to break that ambiguity, and are now deliberate, durable fixture state this case relies on: FaultyOnArrival has an en-US entry ("Faulty on arrival") and a ru-RU entry ("Брак при получении"), but nothing entered for de-DE. This case queries all THREE cultures for the SAME code in one pass and asserts a genuine three-way contrast -- translated / translated DIFFERENTLY in another culture / falls back to the bare code where nothing was entered -- which a hardcoded-string lookup cannot produce (it would return the SAME text regardless of cultureName) and a lookup that always falls back cannot produce either (en-US and ru-RU would both just read the code). NoLongerNeeded (one of the four codes with nothing entered in ANY culture) is checked in all three calls and must read as its bare code every time, confirming the fallback is per-CODE, not a global off switch. Assert the NAMED return a case created, never a total: other lanes submit returns into the same organization at the same time. {HYPOTHESIS} The expectation is the PR's own: the list filters the OrganizationId snapshot stored on the return, not the buyer's current membership, so a departed buyer's return stays in the organization's list. It is what 3x observed and the PO has not stated it; it is NOT certified here as correct. What would make it real: a PO rule either way. The REST body mirrors seed-org-returns.mjs.

Title: organizationReturns and REST search — a renamed organization keeps its old name on existing returns and on returns created after the rename
Preconditions: Runner-native. No browser. Fixtures are the 3a ORG_RET_* personas (organization AGENT-TEST-Org-RetViewer). Every return a case creates is PER-RUN and is cancelled inline; Return.AttachmentsRequired must be at its default false (else the submit step is BLOCKED, KB-84773559). Assert the NAMED return a case created, never a total: other lanes submit returns into the same organization at the same time. {HYPOTHESIS} Records what is observed after a rename (3x: existing rows keep the old name AND a return created after the rename also gets the old name, because it copies the order's snapshot). It is NOT a verdict that this is right: the PO has not said whether a rename should reach existing or new returns, and there is no re-snapshot path in the product (ABSENT, a finding for the PO). What would make it real: the PO's rule; if the rule is "the current name", the two after_rename assertions flip. The holder-side leg is not testable here: ORG_RET_OTHER_ORG has no holder, so the observation is the Admin REST search (the Admin Organization column reads the same field). The rename is written through PUT /api/organizations with the fields the seeder sets (id, memberType, name, emails); the first live run confirms it drops nothing else, and the name is restored in the same case and in Cleanup. The original name is captured from a return read before the rename.
